title: Archimedes of Syracuse
summary: Archimedes of Syracuse (c. 287–212 BCE) was, in MacTutor's words, the greatest mathematician of his age. The Featured Wikipedia article calls him one of the leading scientists in classical antiquity. MacTutor records that he was killed in 212 BC during the capture of Syracuse by the Romans in the Second Punic War.

uncertainty.note: Both dates are given as c. in the Wikipedia Featured article; the MacTutor page gives 287 BC and 212 BC without a range. Astronomical years: 287 BC = -286, 212 BC = -211. The 'c.' qualifier is kept in as_recorded; no band is invented.

where.historical_name: Syracuse, Sicily; the city was under Roman siege in 212 BC (no polity name beyond that given by the sources opened)

importance.justification: The Featured Wikipedia article's lead describes Archimedes as considered one of the leading scientists, and MacTutor records his death in the Roman capture of Syracuse in 212 BC, a documented event of the Second Punic War. The main ground for score 5 is the lead's characterisation of him as a leading scientist; the sources opened here do not rank him further.

audience_note: Records that he was killed during the Roman capture of Syracuse; the sources opened here give no further detail of the death.
